name: Cryogenic messenger-tagging infrared ion spectroscopy in a 30-45 K trap at 2e-6 mbar
plain_name: Identify a molecule by chilling its ions and shining infrared on them
description: Mass- and mobility-selected ions are stored in a cryogenic ion trap held between 30 and 45 K by a closed-cycle helium cryostat, where a pulsed 20% N2/80% He gas mixture forms weakly bound messenger-tagged complexes at about 2e-6 mbar; a tunable mid-IR source is stepped in 2 cm-1 steps from 990 to 1810 cm-1 and tag loss gives a diagnostic vibrational fingerprint. This is how isomeric small molecules, glycans and drug metabolites are distinguished when mass spectrometry alone cannot.
keywords: Identify a molecule by chilling its ions and shining infrared on them

sources.citation: G. P. Szekeres, J. S. Jordan, J. Riedel, J. Horlebein, G. R. D. Prabhu, M. Götze, S. Daly, S. Warnke, K. Pagel, Cryogenic Gas-phase IR Spectroscopy on a Commercial Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry Platform, Analytical Chemistry 98(20):14800-14808 (2026)

requirements.rationale: The trap is operated between 30 and 45 K, tuned for the analyte; outside that window the messenger tag either does not bind or does not detach cleanly.
Tagging requires the trap to be able to reach 30 K; a machine with a higher base temperature cannot condense the N2 messenger onto the ions.
The ions are stored in an evacuated trap chamber; the experiment is impossible in an atmospheric-pressure cold space.
Typical operation is at about 2e-6 mbar inside the trap chamber, so the machine must pump at least that low with the tagging gas pulsed in.
The tunable mid-IR beam has to enter the cold trap and overlap the stored ion cloud, which requires an optical window into the cold space.
Optional: the trap is cooled by a closed-cycle helium cryostat with a single-stage coldhead, so no liquid cryogen is consumed; a bath-cooled implementation would also reach the required temperature.
